Storage

You cannot just make things and not think about where they go. The godown holds 8,27,000 L when it is working properly. On 15 of the 31 days in August it stood at the 95% line.

Why the sheet says 56% and the floor says 112%

  1. 1.SAP takes stock off the books the moment the invoice is cut.
  2. 2.The truck leaves a day or two later. Until it does, those cartons are still standing on our floor.
  3. 3.So the sheet reads 56% full while the floor is at 112%, and the space you were promised is not there.
  4. 4.Stock leaves by two doors, not one — the customer's truck at the dock, and the transfer to Mart. Count both.
  5. 5.Plan production against the floor number, never the book number.
On 1 August the book showed 4,61,225 L on hand (55.8%). By the end of that day the floor held 9,28,314 L (112.3%). The 4,67,089 L gap is two things: 4,67,346 L billed but not yet trucked, plus 0 L made that day net of what shipped. The invoice lag is most of the gap, not all of it.

This is a replay, not a record. It shows what the planner would have done in August 2026, standing on each morning with no later data. The factory did not run this way.
Measured: the order book, opening stock, BOMs, line speeds, realise (May–Jul), lead times, storage ceiling, and the people. Assumed: supply arrives exactly on lead time; a 2-day invoice→truck lag; rated line speed rather than the 47% observed. WhatsApp replies are written in by the simulation, not received.
Every number traces to sim/sim-inputs.json.
